subject: SLA: Cutover maintenance overlap — probe attribution and responsibility
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@orchidhealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@orchidhealth.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Incident during cutover — probe attribution question

Hi Nikhil,

During our cutover on 2026-10-29 (22:00-23:30 UTC) we observed a sustained partial degradation of inference responses — elevated 95th percentile latency and ~6% error rate for the north-svc tenant. Your post-incident summary marks the window as "customer-managed cutover" and excludes it from SLA calculations. Orchids' on-call is confident the degradation began while Redwood had an active routing change that coincided with our traffic shift.

We attached our probe CSV and the cutover schedule. Please confirm how Redwood determined ownership of the window and why it was excluded from the uptime tally. If this is considered a Redwood-maintained routing change that impacted availability, we will request a credit per our contract (DH-9284).

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Sr. SRE, Orchid Health
ops-team@orchidhealth.com

Attachments: probe_trace-2026-10-29.csv (CSV), cutover-schedule-10-29.pdf (PDF)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Incident during cutover — probe attribution question

Alex —

Thanks for the detail and the artifacts. I routed this to our SRE and Routing teams to validate timelines. At a high level: Redwood classifies the event as "customer-cutover overlap" because (a) the traffic shift was initiated from your side per the attached schedule, and (b) control-plane routing changes that occurred in the same window were limited to a canary we rolled to handle a known peering patch.

That said, we do not want to be dismissive — if our routing canary materially increased request failures or latency we will take responsibility. Marissa is pulling logs and the KV probe stacks and will share a timestamped correlation. I put Monica on to line up a short post-mortem call; can you do tomorrow 10:00 AM PT?

Next steps:
- Marissa: validate packet-level routing flip timestamps vs. Alex's probe times.
- Monica: schedule call and ensure we have the SLA ledger export.

Appreciate your patience.

— Nikhil Sharma
Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@orchidhealth.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Incident during cutover — probe attribution question

Alex — attaching our correlation findings. Short summary:

- Redwood routing canary started at 22:07 UTC and completed rolling at 22:14 UTC.
- Orchid's traffic shift begins at 22:05 UTC per your schedule and shows a gradual ramp until 22:22 UTC.
- Our per-shard logs show increased tail latency beginning at ~22:09 UTC with error spikes on shard north-03 at 22:11–22:18 UTC.
- Packet-level traces indicate a transient reconnection loop between Redwood's egress and downstream peering X for ~90 seconds starting at 22:11 UTC; that correlates with the error spike.

Interpretation: there is an overlap where both actions were in flight. Based on our policy, when Redwood-originated control-plane changes produce reconnection loops that coincide with customer traffic shifts, we treat the interval as "shared-impact" and apply proportional apportionment rather than full exclusion. For the window 22:09–22:18 UTC we calculated Redwood's contribution as 58% of error-weighted impact. See the attached CSV for per-minute attributions.

If you prefer a different attribution model (e.g., full-customer-responsibility for cutovers) we can present the options, but contract DH-9284 specifies apportionment for overlapping maintenance and control-plane actions.

Would you be available for the call at 10:00 AM PT tomorrow?

Attachments: redwood-probe-correlation-2026-10-29.csv (CSV)

— Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Reliability
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Nov 2026 16:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Incident during cutover — probe attribution question

Marissa / Nikhil —

Thanks for the quick analysis and the apportionment CSV. Orchids reviewed the minute-level slices and we have two asks:

1) Could Redwood recompute the apportionment using weighted-client-ramp rather than error-weighted attribution? The reason: our traffic ramp shows a sharp spike at 22:22 UTC where our traffic surge likely amplified transient packet drops; we think that will reduce Redwood's percentage contribution for earlier minutes.

2) If the recomputed apportionment still assigns >=40% of the error-weighted impact to Redwood, we'll submit a formal credit request per DH-9284. Please advise timeline for a recompute and the format you need.

We're okay with the scheduled call but would prefer to have a revised attribution before the meeting so we can close faster.

Appreciate the collaboration — we want to avoid a protracted dispute and prefer a mechanical recompute.

Best,
Alex
Sr. SRE, Orchid Health
